questions.stem: Determine the enzyme that is competitively inhibited by statin drugs.
questions.why: Statins are structural analogs of HMG-CoA. They competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis.

notes.B: AMPK inactivates the reductase by phosphorylation; it is not the statin target.
notes.C: AMPK kinase activates AMPK; statins do not act on it.
notes.D: The phosphatase reactivates the reductase; statins do not bind it.
notes.E: PKA works through hormone signalling, not as the statin target.

questions.stem: Which of these enzymes deactivates HMG-CoA Reductase?
questions.why: AMPK acts as a cellular energy sensor. When cellular energy is low, it phosphorylates HMG-CoA reductase, which inactivates the enzyme.

notes.A: The enzyme cannot inactivate itself.
notes.C: AMPK kinase activates AMPK, which then acts on the reductase; it does not act directly.
notes.D: The phosphatase removes the phosphate and so ACTIVATES the reductase.
notes.E: PKA acts indirectly, by inhibiting the phosphatase; AMPK is the direct inactivator.

questions.stem: Which enzyme activates AMP activated kinase?
questions.why: Upstream kinases (such as LKB1 or CaMKKβ) phosphorylate AMPK to activate it.

notes.A: HMG-CoA reductase is the end target, not an activator of AMPK.
notes.B: AMPK cannot activate itself; an upstream kinase phosphorylates it.
notes.D: The phosphatase acts on the reductase, not on AMPK.
notes.E: PKA is not the activator of AMPK.

questions.stem: cAMP indirectly deactivates HMG-CoA Reductase, through which protein is this effect mediated?
questions.why: Glucagon/epinephrine increases cAMP, which activates PKA. PKA initiates a cascade that keeps HMG-CoA reductase phosphorylated and inactive.

notes.A: The reductase is the target being inactivated, not the mediator.
notes.B: AMPK responds to low energy (AMP), not to cAMP.
notes.C: AMPK kinase is not activated by cAMP.
notes.D: The phosphatase is what PKA switches off; it does not carry the cAMP signal itself.

questions.stem: The rate-limiting step in fatty acid synthesis is:

options.label: C
options.text: formation of malonyl-CoA from malonate and coenzyme A.

options.label: D
options.text: the reaction catalyzed by acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

options.label: E
options.text: the reduction of the acetoacetyl group to a β-hydroxybutyryl group

questions.why: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) catalyzes the committed, rate-limiting step of fatty acid synthesis.

notes.A: The condensation is a later step and not the controlled one.
notes.B: Acetyl-CoA comes from citrate (ATP-citrate lyase), and that is not the rate-limiting step.
notes.C: Malonyl-CoA is made by carboxylating acetyl-CoA, not from malonate.
notes.E: This reduction occurs inside fatty acid synthase and is not regulated.

questions.stem: The biosynthesis of triacylglycerols from acetate occurs mainly in:

options.label: B
options.text: humans after ingestion of excess carbohydrate.

questions.why: Excess dietary carbohydrates are converted to acetyl-CoA and then to triacylglycerols for storage in humans.

notes.A: Plants also synthesise triacylglycerols (seed oils).
notes.C: With low carbohydrate intake, fat is broken down rather than made.
notes.D: Animals, including humans, make triacylglycerols.
notes.E: Option B is correct.

questions.stem: Which of these statements about triacylglycerol synthesis is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Humans can store more energy in glycogen than in triacylglycerols.

options.label: B
options.text: Insulin stimulates conversion of dietary carbohydrate into triacylglycerols.

options.label: C
options.text: It is not a hormone-sensitive process.

options.label: D
options.text: Mammals are unable to convert carbohydrates into triacylglycerols.

options.label: E
options.text: Phosphatidate is not on the pathway of triacylglycerol synthesis.

questions.why: Insulin promotes lipogenesis (converting carbs to fat) and inhibits lipolysis.

notes.A: Fat stores far more energy than glycogen.
notes.C: It is hormone-sensitive: insulin promotes it.
notes.D: Mammals readily convert excess carbohydrate to fat.
notes.E: Phosphatidate is a key intermediate of triacylglycerol synthesis.

questions.stem: A strategy that is not employed in the synthesis of phospholipids is:

options.label: D
options.text: exchange of free alcohol with head group alcohol of phospholipid.

options.label: E
options.text: remodeling of head group alcohols by chemical modification

questions.why: Phospholipid synthesis involves CDP-activated intermediates, but not condensation of two CDP-linked molecules.

notes.A: This IS used, e.g. CDP-choline + DAG → phosphatidylcholine.
notes.B: This IS used, e.g. CDP-DAG + inositol → phosphatidylinositol.
notes.D: Head-group exchange IS used, e.g. serine exchange for ethanolamine.
notes.E: Head-group modification IS used, e.g. methylating PE to PC.

questions.stem: The major source of cholesterol in arterial smooth muscle cells is from:
questions.why: LDL delivers cholesterol to peripheral tissues via receptor-mediated endocytosis.

notes.A: IDL is mostly converted to LDL or taken up by the liver.
notes.C: HDL removes cholesterol from tissues (reverse transport).
notes.D: Chylomicrons carry dietary fat; their remnants go to the liver.
notes.E: VLDL mainly carries triglyceride and becomes LDL.

questions.stem: Endogenous triglycerides in plasma is maximally bound to:
questions.why: VLDL transports endogenously synthesized triglycerides from the liver.

notes.A: Chylomicrons carry EXOGENOUS (dietary) triglyceride.
notes.B: LDL is cholesterol-rich, not triglyceride-rich.
notes.D: HDL carries little triglyceride.
notes.E: IDL is a partly emptied VLDL remnant.

questions.stem: The precursor of cholesterol synthesis is:
questions.why: All 27 carbons of cholesterol are derived from acetyl-CoA.

notes.A: Acetate must first be activated to acetyl-CoA.
notes.C: Oxaloacetate is a TCA cycle intermediate, not the sterol precursor.
notes.D: Malate is a TCA cycle intermediate.
notes.E: Pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA first.

questions.stem: All are derived of cholesterol except:
questions.why: Cholecystokinin is a peptide hormone from the duodenum, made from amino acids. Bile acids (chenodeoxycholic and glycocholic acid), steroid hormones (testosterone) and vitamin D are all made from cholesterol.

notes.A: Chenodeoxycholic acid is a primary bile acid made from cholesterol.
notes.B: Glycocholic acid is cholic acid (from cholesterol) conjugated with glycine.
notes.C: Testosterone is a steroid hormone made from cholesterol.
notes.D: Vitamin D3 is made from 7-dehydrocholesterol.

questions.stem: Determine the lipoprotein that best detect Lipid profile of a non-fasting patient:
questions.why: Non-fasting blood primarily reflects the presence of dietary chylomicrons.

notes.A: LDL changes little after a meal.
notes.B: VLDL is mainly of liver origin and changes little soon after a meal.
notes.D: IDL is a VLDL remnant and is not meal-dependent.
notes.E: Total cholesterol is not a lipoprotein and changes little after a meal.

questions.stem: Clinically, bile acids are important in:

options.label: B
options.text: enhancing the formation of atherogenic plaques

options.label: C
options.text: inhibition of intestinal absorption of fat soluble vitamins

questions.why: Converting cholesterol to bile acids and excreting them in faeces is the body's main route for getting rid of excess cholesterol (sterol). Bile acids emulsify fats; they do not precipitate them, they do not promote plaques, they are needed FOR fat-soluble vitamin absorption, and they do not cause fatty liver.

notes.A: Bile acids emulsify fats; they do not precipitate them.
notes.B: Bile acid loss lowers cholesterol, so it opposes plaque formation.
notes.C: Bile acids are needed FOR fat-soluble vitamin absorption.
notes.D: Bile acids do not cause fatty liver.

questions.stem: A person with a type IIA hyperlipoproteinemia had a blood cholesterol level of 360 mg/dL and blood triglyceride levels of 140 mg/dL. This person most likely has:

options.label: A
options.text: an increased ability to produce VLDL

options.label: B
options.text: a decreased ability for receptor-mediated endocytosis of LDL

options.label: C
options.text: an elevation of HDL in the blood

options.label: D
options.text: a decreased ability to convert VLDL to IDL

questions.why: Type IIA is familial hypercholesterolemia, typically due to defective LDL receptors, preventing LDL clearance.

notes.A: Overproduction of VLDL would raise triglycerides too (type IIb/IV).
notes.C: Raised HDL does not produce this picture.
notes.D: A block of VLDL → IDL conversion would raise triglycerides.

questions.stem: A person with a low-density lipoprotein (LDL) receptor deficiency was treated with lovastatin. As a consequence of the action of this drug, the person should have:

options.label: A
options.text: fewer LDL receptors in cell membranes

questions.why: Statins lower intracellular cholesterol, causing cells to upregulate LDL receptors, which clears LDL from the blood.

notes.A: Statins INCREASE LDL receptor numbers.
notes.B: Statins DECREASE de novo cholesterol synthesis.
notes.C: Less cholesterol in the cell means LESS ACAT activity.
notes.E: Statins do not raise triacylglycerols.

questions.stem: Arrange the following lipoproteins in increasing order of density:
questions.why: Density rises as the lipid:protein ratio falls: chylomicrons < VLDL < IDL < LDL < HDL. None of the listed sequences follows that order.

notes.A: LDL is denser than VLDL, so it cannot come before it.
notes.B: HDL is the densest, so it cannot sit in the middle.
notes.C: VLDL is lighter than IDL, so this order is wrong.
notes.D: This is DECREASING density.

questions.stem:
During fatty acid synthesis, the growing acyl chain is covalently attached to which of the following? Key:
I. NADPH
II. β-keto-acyl:ACP reductase
III. enoyl-ACP reductase
IV. ACP1 and ACP2
V. ACP-acyl transferase
questions.why: The growing chain is held as a thioester on the acyl carrier protein arms (the pantetheinyl -SH of ACP and the cysteinyl -SH of the condensing enzyme, called ACP1 and ACP2 in this course). NADPH and the reductases act on the chain but do not carry it.

notes.A: Includes I, which is false, and leaves out IV, which is true.
notes.B: Includes I and II, which are false, and leaves out IV, which is true.
notes.C: Includes I and III, which are false, and leaves out IV, which is true.
notes.E: Includes I, II and III, which are false, and leaves out IV, which is true.

questions.stem: Transfers Acetyl group from CoA to cysteinyl-S on ACP.
questions.why: Acetyl-CoA: ACP transacylase transfers the acetyl group from Coenzyme A to the active site of the ACP.

notes.A: NADPH is a reducing agent, not a transferase.
notes.B: ACP is the carrier, not the enzyme that loads it.
notes.C: ACP is the carrier, not the enzyme that loads it.
notes.D: The reductase reduces the β-keto group; it does not transfer acetyl groups.

questions.stem: Transfers Malonyl group from CoA to pantetheinyl-S on ACP.
questions.why: Malonyl-CoA: ACP transacylase transfers the malonyl group to the phosphopantetheine arm of the ACP.

notes.A: NADPH is a reducing agent, not a transferase.
notes.B: ACP is the carrier, not the enzyme that loads it.
notes.C: ACP is the carrier, not the enzyme that loads it.
notes.D: The reductase reduces the β-keto group; it does not transfer malonyl groups.

questions.stem: In this reaction CO2 departs from malonylCoA reducing ACP. Which enzyme catalyzes this?
questions.why: The condensation reaction joins the acetyl and malonyl groups, decarboxylating the malonyl group to release CO2. This is catalyzed by Keto Acyl: ACP synthase.

notes.A: ACP is a carrier, not an enzyme.
notes.B: ACP is a carrier, not an enzyme.
notes.C: The transacylase only loads malonyl onto ACP.
notes.E: Thioesterase releases the finished palmitate.

questions.stem:
Reduction of the keto group to an alcohol requires: Key:
I. NADPH
II. β-keto-acyl:ACP reductase
III. enoyl-ACP reductase
IV. ACP1 and ACP2
V. ACP-acyl transferase
questions.why: The enzyme β-keto-Acyl: ACP reductase (II) reduces the keto group to a hydroxyl group, and it requires NADPH (I).

notes.A: Leaves out II, which is also true.
notes.C: Includes III, which is false, and leaves out II, which is true.
notes.D: Includes IV, which is false, and leaves out I and II, which are true.
notes.E: Includes III, which is false.

questions.stem:
The enoyl group is reduced to a saturated group by: Key:
I. NADPH
II. β-keto-acyl:ACP reductase
III. enoyl-ACP reductase
IV. ACP1 and ACP2
V. ACP-acyl transferase
questions.why: Enoyl-ACP reductase (III) reduces the double bond to a single bond, utilizing NADPH (I).

notes.A: Leaves out III, which is also true.
notes.B: Includes II, which is false, and leaves out III, which is true.
notes.D: Includes IV, which is false, and leaves out I and III, which are true.
notes.E: Includes II, which is false.

questions.stem: Most potent reducing agent in fatty acid synthesis:
questions.why: NADPH provides the reducing power for the two reduction steps in fatty acid synthesis.

notes.B: ACP carries the chain; it donates no electrons.
notes.C: ACP carries the chain; it donates no electrons.
notes.D: The reductase uses NADPH; it is not itself the reducing agent.
notes.E: The transferase moves acyl groups; it does not reduce.

questions.stem: What constitutes the substrate-carrying arm of the synthase complex:
questions.why: The Acyl Carrier Protein (ACP) holds the growing fatty acid chain during synthesis.

notes.B: ACP II is not the substrate-carrying arm in this scheme.
notes.C: The transferase is an enzyme that loads the arm, not the arm itself.
notes.D: Thioesterase releases the product.
notes.E: NADPH is the reductant, not a carrier.

questions.stem: Deficiency of lipoprotein lipase may not give rise to the following clinical manifestation:
questions.why: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency causes hypertriglyceridemia, hepatosplenomegaly, and xanthomas, but not muscular dystrophy.

notes.A: Hepatosplenomegaly IS a feature, from lipid-laden macrophages.
notes.B: Abdominal pain IS a feature (pancreatitis from very high chylomicrons).
notes.C: Eruptive xanthomata ARE a feature.
notes.D: Lack of lipase activity in post-heparin plasma IS the diagnostic finding.

questions.stem: Type III hyperlipidemia is caused by a deficiency in apoprotein E. Analysis of the serum of patient with this disorder would exhibit which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: An absence of chylomicrons after eating

options.label: B
options.text: Normal levels of VLDL after eating

questions.why: ApoE is needed for the liver to take up chylomicron remnants and IDL. Without it these remnants accumulate, so both triglycerides and cholesterol are raised (type III, dysbetalipoproteinaemia).

notes.A: Chylomicrons still form; their remnants are cleared poorly.
notes.B: VLDL remnants build up, so levels are not normal.
notes.C: Triglycerides are raised.
notes.D: Cholesterol is raised, not lowered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of the fatty acid elongation system of vertebrate cells?

options.label: A
options.text: It involves the same four-step sequence seen in the fatty acid synthase complex.

options.label: B
options.text: It is located in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

options.label: C
options.text: It produces stearoyl-CoA by the extension of palmitoyl-CoA.

options.label: D
options.text: It uses malonyl-CoA as a substrate.

options.label: E
options.text: The immediate precursor of the added carbons is acetyl-CoA.

questions.why: The immediate precursor of added carbons is malonyl-CoA, not acetyl-CoA.

notes.A: True: it repeats condensation, reduction, dehydration and reduction.
notes.B: True: elongases sit in the smooth ER.
notes.C: True: palmitoyl-CoA (C16) is extended to stearoyl-CoA (C18).
notes.D: True: malonyl-CoA donates the 2-carbon units.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of the differences between fatty acid synthesis and fatty acid β-oxidation?

options.label: A
options.text: A thioester derivative of crotonic acid (trans-2-butenoic acid) is an intermediate in the synthetic path, but not in the degradative path.

options.label: B
options.text: A thioester derivative of D-β-hydroxybutyrate is an intermediate in the synthetic path, not in the degradative path.

options.label: C
options.text: Fatty acid synthesis uses NADPH, whereas β-oxidation produces NADH and FADH2.

options.label: D
options.text: Fatty acid degradation is catalysed by cytosolic enzymes; fatty acid synthesis by mitochondrial enzymes.

options.label: E
options.text: The condensation of two acetyl-CoA molecules in a crude extract is faster in bicarbonate buffer than in phosphate buffer at the same pH.

questions.why: It is the reverse: fatty acid synthesis is cytosolic and β-oxidation is mitochondrial. The other statements are true (synthesis uses the D-isomer and NADPH; bicarbonate is needed for acetyl-CoA carboxylase).

notes.A: True: crotonyl-ACP is a synthetic intermediate; β-oxidation uses the CoA form.
notes.B: True: synthesis uses the D-isomer, β-oxidation the L-isomer.
notes.C: True: this is a real difference between the two paths.
notes.E: True: bicarbonate supplies CO2 for acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

questions.stem: A healthy 70-year-old man is told to fast for 12 hours before his plasma lipids are measured, but he eats a large breakfast 3 hours before the blood draw. Which change is most likely?
questions.why: Dietary fat is carried from the gut as chylomicrons, so a recent meal sharply raises chylomicrons and plasma triglycerides. LDL- and HDL-cholesterol change very little after one meal, which is why triglycerides need a fasting sample.

notes.B: LDL changes very little after one meal.
notes.C: HDL changes very little after one meal.
notes.D: VLDL does not fall after a meal.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Friedewald equation is considered fairly accurate and widely employed.
Reason: some factors that could cause deviations in the Friedewald equation are unaccounted for using this calculation.
questions.why: Both are true. The Friedewald equation (LDL = TC − HDL − TG/5 in mg/dL) is widely used because it is simple and cheap, and it does ignore factors (e.g. TG above about 4.5 mmol/L, chylomicrons) that make it inaccurate. But those limitations do not explain why it is considered accurate, so the reason is not the explanation.

notes.A: Wrong here: the reason does not explain the assertion.
notes.C: Wrong here: the reason is true.
notes.D: Wrong here: the assertion is true.
notes.E: Wrong here: the assertion is true and the reason is true.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Hypertriglyceridemia may lead to Pancreatitis.
Reason: excessively elevated levels of chylomicrons from diet can cause occlusion of the capillaries leading to ischaemia and local acidaemia which can expose triglycerides to pancreatic lipases whose effect is the degradation of triglycerides to free fatty acids, causing to cytotoxic injury.
questions.why: Both statements are true. High chylomicrons cause capillary occlusion, leading to ischemia and acidosis, which activates pancreatic lipases to release toxic free fatty acids.

notes.B: Wrong here: the reason does explain the assertion.
notes.C: Wrong here: the reason is true.
notes.D: Wrong here: the assertion is true.
notes.E: Wrong here: the assertion is true and the reason is true.

questions.stem: Enzymes that catalyze the synthesis of long chain fatty acids in vertebrate cells:

options.label: C
options.text: are localized in the mitochondrial matrix.

options.label: D
options.text: are part of a single polypeptide chain containing several distinct enzyme activities.

options.label: E
options.text: have none of the characteristics above.

questions.why: In vertebrates, fatty acid synthase is a multifunctional megaprotein.

notes.A: That is the bacterial (type II) system, not vertebrates.
notes.B: Fatty acid synthase is encoded by nuclear DNA.
notes.C: Fatty acid synthesis is cytosolic.
notes.E: Option D is correct.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of the fatty acid synthasis and the fatty acid β-oxidation systems?

options.label: A
options.text: A derivative of the vitamin pantothenic acid is involved.

options.label: C
options.text: Double bonds are oxidized or reduced by pyridine nucleotide coenzymes.

options.label: D
options.text: The processes occur in different cellular compartments.

options.label: E
options.text: The processes occur in the mitochondrial matrix.

questions.why: Fatty acid synthesis occurs in the cytosol; only beta-oxidation occurs in the mitochondria.

notes.A: Both use a pantothenate derivative (CoA, and the ACP arm).
notes.B: Acyl-CoA (or acyl-ACP) derivatives are intermediates in both.
notes.C: NAD(P) reduces or oxidises the double bonds in both.
notes.D: True: synthesis is cytosolic and β-oxidation mitochondrial.

questions.stem: HMG CoA reductase is inhibited by:
questions.why: Lovastatin is a statin, which competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase.

notes.A: Clofibrate is a fibrate that acts on PPAR-α.
notes.B: Gemfibrozil is a fibrate that acts on PPAR-α.
notes.D: Cholestyramine binds bile acids in the gut.
notes.E: Lovastatin does inhibit it.

questions.stem: Atherosclerosis can be managed by the following drug treatment:
questions.why: Simvastatin, a statin, inhibits HMG-CoA reductase and is the main drug for lowering LDL in atherosclerosis. Niacin works only at high doses, and diet or surgery are not drug treatments.

notes.A: Niacin lowers lipids only at high doses.
notes.B: Vitamin C has no proven role in treating atherosclerosis.
notes.C: Surgery is not a drug treatment.
notes.D: Diet is not a drug treatment.

questions.stem: Atherosclerotic plaques development cannot be accelerated under the following pathological conditions:

options.label: A
options.text: The consumption of high fat diets

questions.why: HDL is cardioprotective and prevents plaque formation.

notes.A: A high-fat diet raises LDL and speeds up plaque formation.
notes.B: Oxidised LDL is taken up by macrophages to form foam cells.
notes.C: Small dense LDL is highly atherogenic.
notes.E: High LDL in familial hypercholesterolaemia speeds up plaque formation.

questions.stem: The clinical importance of apolipoproteins:

options.label: A
options.text: Solubilization of lipids in the gut

options.label: C
options.text: Can inactivate some lipid metabolic enzymes

options.label: D
options.text: Prevents the cholestasis of bile salts

questions.why: ApoB-100 and ApoE act as ligands for receptors.

notes.A: Bile salts solubilise lipids in the gut, not apolipoproteins.
notes.C: Apolipoproteins mainly ACTIVATE enzymes (e.g. C-II for lipoprotein lipase).
notes.D: Cholestasis is not prevented by apolipoproteins.
notes.E: Lipidoses are lysosomal enzyme defects, not apolipoprotein disorders.

questions.stem: Which apoprotein is the main structural protein of VLDL?
questions.why: Apo B-100 is the structural protein of VLDL (and IDL and LDL) and the ligand for the LDL receptor. Apo B-48 belongs to chylomicrons and Apo A-I to HDL; VLDL picks up C-II and E from HDL, but they are not its structural protein.

notes.B: Apo B-48 is the structural protein of chylomicrons.
notes.C: Apo A-I is the main HDL protein.
notes.D: Apo C-II is acquired from HDL and activates lipoprotein lipase.
notes.E: Apo E is acquired and helps remnant uptake; it is not structural.

questions.stem: The most important long-term clinical consequence of persistently raised plasma VLDL is:
questions.why: VLDL and its remnants are atherogenic, so persistently high VLDL promotes atherosclerosis. Hepatosplenomegaly and abdominal pain (pancreatitis) are features of very high chylomicrons, and lipoprotein lipase deficiency is a cause, not a consequence.

notes.B: High VLDL does not lower cholesterol.
notes.C: Hepatosplenomegaly goes with very high chylomicrons.
notes.D: Abdominal pain (pancreatitis) goes with very high chylomicrons.
notes.E: Lipoprotein lipase deficiency is a cause, not a consequence.

questions.stem: Lipidoses:

options.label: A
options.text: are acquired diseases of catabolism of lipids

options.label: B
options.text: there is deficiency of the respective lipid substrate in the nervous system and/or peripheral tissues

options.label: C
options.text: there is accumulation of lipid substrate in the stomach resulting in obesity

options.label: D
options.text: the clinical chemical diagnosis can be accomplished by demonstration of the enzyme defect

options.label: E
options.text: the clinical chemical diagnosis cannot be accomplished by the demonstration of substrate accumulation in body fluids

questions.why: Lipidoses (lipid storage diseases) are diagnosed by demonstrating the specific enzyme defect.

notes.A: They are inherited enzyme defects.
notes.B: The substrate ACCUMULATES; it is not deficient.
notes.C: Storage is in tissues such as the brain, liver and spleen, not the stomach.
notes.E: Substrate accumulation CAN support the diagnosis.

questions.stem: Mechanism of action of drugs regulating Familial hypercholestolaemia:

options.label: A
options.text: Cholestyramine: combines with bile acids and prevent cholesterol reabsorption

options.label: B
options.text: Cholestyramine: combines with lipoprotein lipase and prevent cholesterol reabsorption

options.label: C
options.text: Small doses of niacin prevent cholesterol absorption

options.label: D
options.text: Large doses of niacin prevent cholesterol excretion

questions.why: Cholestyramine is a bile acid sequestrant.

notes.B: Cholestyramine binds bile acids, not an enzyme.
notes.C: Niacin works only at high doses.
notes.D: Niacin reduces VLDL production; it does not block cholesterol excretion.
notes.E: Sitosterol competes with dietary cholesterol for absorption.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman has a mild heart attack and is placed on diet and statin therapy. What will be the most likely result of this therapy?
questions.why: Statins lower LDL levels, reducing the risk of further cardiovascular events.

notes.A: Statins LOWER cholesterol.
notes.B: Statins do not lower blood glucose.
notes.D: Statins do not act on fatty acid oxidation.
notes.E: Statins LOWER LDL.

questions.stem: Type I hyperlipidemia may be caused by a deficiency of apoprotein C-II. What would be exhibited by analysis of the serum of patients with this disorder?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher than normal levels of VLDL after eating

questions.why: ApoC-II is required for lipoprotein lipase to clear chylomicrons and VLDL, so a deficiency leads to elevated triglycerides.

notes.A: VLDL clearance is also slowed, but the defining finding is raised triglycerides.
notes.B: Triglycerides are raised.
notes.D: Cholesterol is usually normal or only mildly raised.
notes.E: Triglycerides are raised, not lowered.

questions.stem: Lipoprotein particle metabolism can occur:

options.label: A
options.text: via the exogenous or endogenous pathway,

options.label: B
options.text: Independent of the source of origin.

questions.why: Lipoproteins are metabolized via exogenous (dietary) and endogenous (hepatic) pathways.

notes.B: The pathway depends on whether the lipid is dietary or made in the liver.
notes.C: Bile is needed to absorb dietary lipid.
notes.D: Lipoproteins are also processed in the intestine, plasma and tissues.

questions.stem: Lipoproteins are characterized based on their various proportions which determine their by their density. Which one of the following sequences places the lipoproteins in the order of most dense to least dense?
questions.why: The correct order from most dense to least dense is HDL > LDL > VLDL > Chylomicrons.

notes.A: VLDL is not denser than LDL.
notes.C: HDL is the densest, not third.
notes.D: This is roughly the reverse.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Atherosclerosis is a disease where capillary walls become less elastic and thicker.
Reason: fatty materials accumulate beneath the outer lining of the capillary wall.
questions.why: Both are false. Atherosclerosis affects arteries (not capillaries), and lipid accumulates beneath the INNER lining (intima), not the outer lining.

notes.A: Wrong here: the assertion is false and the reason is false.
notes.B: Wrong here: the assertion is false and the reason is false.
notes.C: Wrong here: the assertion is false.
notes.D: Wrong here: the reason is false.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Bile salts are not essential to lipid metabolism.
Reason: bile salts can be produced by the body.
questions.why: The assertion is false; bile salts are essential for emulsifying lipids. The reason is true.

notes.A: Wrong here: the assertion is false.
notes.B: Wrong here: the assertion is false.
notes.C: Wrong here: the assertion is false and the reason is true.
notes.E: Wrong here: the reason is true.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase may not be the most desirable method for controlling cholesterol levels.
Reason: mevalonate is needed for the synthesis of important molecules such as acetyl CoA.
questions.why: The assertion is true. The reason is false: mevalonate is a precursor for cholesterol, CoQ10, and dolichol, but not acetyl CoA.

notes.A: Wrong here: the reason is false.
notes.B: Wrong here: the reason is false.
notes.D: Wrong here: the assertion is true and the reason is false.
notes.E: Wrong here: the assertion is true.

questions.stem: Kofi, a 35-year-old, has been diagnosed with severe hypercholesterolaemia. Which of the following plasma cholesterol levels would indicate this condition?

options.label: E
options.text: Patient may not suffer from heart attack

questions.why: A total plasma cholesterol greater than 7.0 mmol/L is a definitive indicator of severe hypercholesterolemia.

notes.B: Low bile salts affect fat digestion; this is not a cholesterol level.
notes.C: This describes fat malabsorption, not a cholesterol level.
notes.D: Reductase deficiency would LOWER cholesterol.
